data.narrative: Alekhya navigated the high-pressure mock incident in Module 05 with remarkable poise and professional discipline. She correctly classified the active auth bypass data deletion as a critical SEV1 incident, held firm under executive pressure without minimizing the breach, and delivered transparent, structured updates within 4 minutes. Technically, she closed Bug #8 by implementing defense-in-depth Authorization header validation in get_current_admin across all 5 verification scenarios, while formulating a 5-step PITR backup restoration plan to recover the 12 deleted links without permanent data loss.

dimension_scores.observation: Delivered structured, plain-language stakeholder updates adhering to the 5-minute SLA, answering the prospect demo question directly and de-escalating panic.
dimension_scores.evidence: We are investigating unauthorized access to our admin API... public redirect service is on a separate endpoint and is NOT affected. Next update in 10 minutes.

dimension_scores.observation: Recognized that 47 unauthorized DELETE requests returning 200 from an unrecognized IP constituted active exploitation of an auth bypass; fixed empty/whitespace header validation.
dimension_scores.evidence: 47 unauthorized deletions returning 200 is not a theoretical vulnerability or brute force, but active exploitation of an auth bypass. Classified as SEV1.

dimension_scores.observation: Maintained focus on customer blast radius; prioritized continuous database WAL Point-In-Time-Recovery (PITR) at 14:20:00 UTC and proactive customer notifications over silence.
dimension_scores.evidence: Structured a 5-step recovery: query PITR backup at 14:20:00 UTC, extract the 12 rows, transactional re-insert, test 302 resolution, and proactively notify the 8 affected users.

dimension_scores.observation: Reasoned through communicating first vs fixing first, establishing official communication within 5 minutes to prevent chaotic escalations while isolating the vulnerability.
dimension_scores.evidence: Communicate first within 5 minutes: acknowledges the incident, prevents chaotic executive escalations, establishes the official communication log, and gives responders focused time to debug safely.

dimension_scores.observation: Rigorously verified the fix across 5 edge-case header states (empty string, whitespace, missing token, valid token, missing header) and raw socket requests.
dimension_scores.evidence: scripts/verify_incident_auth.py proved all 5 scenarios return 401/200 and raw socket DELETE returned HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

strengths: Crisis communication composure: delivers clear, honest stakeholder updates without sugarcoating data loss or panicking non-technical leadership.
Defense-in-depth auth hardening: validates presence, structure, token existence, and cryptographic signature to eliminate falsy/whitespace bypasses.
Incident aftermath accountability: recognizes that closing the vulnerability is only step one; formulates precise PITR recovery and transparent customer outreach.
growth_areas: Preparing for complex multi-layer distributed system bugs and cascading retry storms across queue workers and caches in Module 06.
data.recommendation: Advance to Interlude 04 (2003 Northeast Blackout) and Module 06: Multi-Layer Bugs.

public_evidence.student_action: Patched Bug #8 admin auth bypass vulnerability, hardening Authorization header parsing against empty string and whitespace-only exploits; drafted PITR recovery plan for 12 deleted links.
public_evidence.technical_detail: FastAPI + Starlette + HMAC SHA256 JWT auth + PostgreSQL WAL PITR recovery + scripts/verify_incident_auth.py
public_evidence.proof: All 5 header verification test cases returned HTTP 401/200; raw socket DELETE test confirmed HTTP 401; 64/64 pytest tests passed; recovery plan verified for 14:20:00 UTC snapshot
public_evidence.ability: Incident triage, crisis stakeholder communication, authentication defense-in-depth, and disaster data recovery
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates composure during active security incidents: communicating transparently under executive pressure, rapidly patching auth bypass vulnerabilities, and recovering deleted data
